text.text:
Located right along Hollywood Boulevard, this In-N-Out Burger is one of the most iconic fast-food stops for both locals and tourists. The restaurant is almost always bustling with customers, with long lines inside and a constant stream of cars filling the drive-thru. During peak lunch and dinner hours, the drive-thru line often extends onto the nearby streets, so expect a wait whether you’re ordering in person or from your car.

The menu features all of In-N-Out’s classic favorites, including the Double-Double, Cheeseburger, Hamburger, and even the 3×3 (Triple-Triple) for those with a bigger appetite. Sides include their famous French Fries and Animal Style Fries, while drinks range from soft drinks and iced tea to their signature lemonade and light lemonade.

One thing I especially enjoy is adding fresh lemon slices to my drink, which gives the lemonade or iced tea an even fresher and more refreshing flavor.

Another reason In-N-Out remains so popular is the wide range of customization options. You can order grilled onions, Animal Style burgers and fries, the famous Flying Dutchman from the not-so-secret menu, or finish your meal with a Neapolitan shake, which combines chocolate, vanilla, and strawberry flavors into one drink. They also provide pickled jalapeños upon request, adding a nice spicy kick for those who enjoy extra heat.

Despite how crowded this location gets, the operation runs impressively smoothly. The staff work hard to keep orders moving, while security helps maintain order during busy periods. Employees are also constantly cleaning the dining area and restrooms, helping the restaurant stay surprisingly tidy despite the nonstop crowds.

One of the biggest advantages of this location is its late-night hours. It’s open until 1:00 a.m. on weekdays and 1:30 a.m. on weekends, making it one of the best places to grab a meal after exploring Hollywood, watching a movie, or enjoying the nightlife. In fact, I find that late at night the lines are often much shorter, making it an excellent time to visit.

Parking at the restaurant is limited, especially during busy hours, but it becomes much easier later in the evening.

It’s a fun story that the director won the Oscar reward quickly went here for dining just after the Oscar ceremony.

Overall, In-N-Out Burger Hollywood delivers exactly what people expect from this iconic California chain: fresh burgers, endless customization options, friendly service, and a lively atmosphere. Whether it’s your first In-N-Out experience or your hundredth, it’s a must-visit stop when exploring Hollywood—and an even better choice if you visit after the crowds begin to thin late at night.

We came here for our triple anniversary. My parents, my sister and her husband, and myself and my wife. We ordered the broccolini, the carrots, the peas, the beef and bone marrow pie, the lamb, grilled octopus, the bistecca fiorentina, the Focaccia de Recco, Caesar salad, and citrus salad. For dessert, we got the cheesecake, the apple pie, and we were treated to a passion fruit sorbet.
I would say our favourites were:
- the Caesar salad
- the carrots
- the broccolini
- the bistecca fiorentina (New York on one side, fillet on the other)
- focaccia de recco
- grilled octopus
I think for seven people, this was more than enough food for everybody to try a little of everything. Nobody was left hungry or wanting for more at the end. This was plenty.
The bistecca fiorentina took an hour and a half. It's a huge cut of meat, so that's fully understandable and well worth the wait.
Service was very, very good, some of the best that I've ever had and quite enjoyable. Everybody was very polite, very nice, had lots of information for us, and was very attentive.
I'm definitely looking forward to coming back and trying even more from their menu. It is very pricey, but I think it's worth it. It's quite the experience.
We all enjoyed the food and enjoyed the experience quite a lot. I highly recommend.
- the beef and bone marrow pie

We were out late after leaving a music venue and needed something to eat.I jumped on Yelp and found Fat Sam's. It's a great late-night spot when those food cravings hit. The décor has a cool club/bar vibe that fits the late-night atmosphere.

I ordered the Philly Cheesesteak Sandwich, and it was pretty good. The meat was tender, the ratio of cheese to onions was just right, and everything worked well together. But the real star of the sandwich was the bread. It was soft, pillowy, and had the perfect amount of chew, bringing the whole sandwich together.

My wife ordered the Chili Cheese Fries, but she wasn't a fan. Her exact words were, "Meh." She felt the chili lacked the depth of flavor she was hoping for.

If you're in the Hollywood area looking for a late-night bite, I'd recommend checking them out. They have a large selection of creative and over the top sandwiches, so there's a good chance you'll find something to please your cravings.

My review is largely based on my standards of what I consider good Italian.
I personally think it is scammy to price yourself as a high quality spot yet you serve boxed pasta and don't even make your own spaghetti. My pasta came undercooked - it happens. But it was crunchy in the middle. Raw fresh pasta is doughy, if the pasta is crunchy then that means it is undercooked boxed pasta.
I also added fresh truffles, I got between 7 and 9 of the thinnest translucent shavings of truffle. It basically was essence of truffle.
Even the fast casual Uovo chain makes their own pasta.
As a side note, other comments about the poor service and seemingly prejudice staff are 100% true. The sketchy street corner they are on fits their attitude perfectly.

This was on par with olive garden quality. Except olive garden is cheaper. When you want high quality italian, I recommend Chi Spacca, Oste on 3rd, or Locanda Ventana down the street from my house. Save your dollars and skip the overpriced boxed pasta.

Thank you, The Benjamin, for restoring my faith in the Los Angeles food scene. I’ll definitely be back—and I’ll be telling people. VAMOS ⚡️⚡️

text.text:
Laurel Hardware is an easy 5/5 for me after this meal. The vibe is laid-back but the food feels way more elevated than your standard night-out spot.

The standout was the butternut squash tortellini – rich, silky sauce, perfectly cooked pasta, and those little pops of flavor in every bite. It hit that comfort-food spot without feeling heavy, and I’d come back just for that bowl alone. The margarita pizza was legit too: blistered crust, great chew, and just the right balance of sauce, cheese, and char so every slice tasted like it came out of a legit wood-fired oven. The strawberry salad rounded everything out with fresh greens, bright acidity, and enough texture to make it feel like a real part of the meal instead of an afterthought.

Service was relaxed but attentive, and it all worked really well with the casual, buzzy patio energy. If you’re into places where you can hang out for a while, share plates, and still feel like you’re eating something a little special, Laurel Hardware absolutely delivers.

Mel's is the quintessential American diner. Housed in a classic 1950s "googie" architecture building, it's a great place to get comfort food in a cool environment.

There's also outdoor seating so you can sit on the famous Sunset strip (and watch traffic and billboards).

The food is uniformly excellent, but not inexpensive (this is an upscale diner). Breakfast is always available and their pancakes are especially good!

The service is friendly, attentive, efficient, and the servers have real personality!

There's FREE valet parking in the back ( a pleasant surprise in LA).

It's also one of the rare restaurants that's open late, Thursday and Friday it's open till 3:00 a.m. And it's 24 hours a day over the weekend.

Tourists and locals alike enjoy this old fashioned slice of Americana. You probably will, too!

It was pretty busy when we went at around 9am but it was lively but not too noisy.

Overall:
A decent breakfast experience where it’s not bad food BUT at $20 for just pancakes, it seems a little high. They do offer a bottomless pancakes option but they’re thick and dense.

text.text:
The sharing plates are modest, but it’s better to have more people to take advantage of variety.

The inside of the restaurant has ambient lighting, but a bit too loud for a casual convo.

Our waiter was wonderful, and offered suggestions for dishes based on preference.  I went with my mom, and we are picky eaters so the list was slightly limited, but there were still great choices.

My favorite dish was the crispy okra, which was only lightly coated, and not slimy at all!  They could garnish salt with a lighter hand, as it piled on only a few pieces.

Black cod is black cod, and they prepared it well.  The piece was thicker and larger than expected.

The hamachi app is garnished with cilantro, but there is no mention of such on the menu.  Easy to pluck off.  The jalapeño slices were moderately spicy, and complemented the ponzu and fish well.

Mushroom side seemed heavy on king oyster (not a favorite), but the maitake and shiitake were flavorful.

Finally, the half lobster tempura was tasty.  The marinade was light enough to still leave the nuggets crisp rather than soggy.

Overall great treat, and better suited for moderate sized groups with strong appetites.
